text:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression in the KV cache hot path after switching the batcher to a dynamic-window heuristic. Trying to capture an nsys trace (cuda,nvtx,osrt) but outputs are massive. Any recommended CLI flags/strategy?

devon: For KV/cache/kernel stuff I usually: keep trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt, restrict duration, and capture only the pid. also use NVTX ranges around the interesting section.

maria: can you paste an example command?

devon: sure — short and pragmatic:

```bash
nsys profile -o kvreg-try1 \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --duration=10s \
  --force-overwrite \
  --pid 43210
```

devon: --sample=cpu reduces event volume vs full instruction sampling. --duration keeps file size bounded. pid filter avoids system noise.

alex: if you can edit the code, add NVTX push/pop around the exact batch processing function and use capture-range (nvtx) so you only capture the inner loop. e.g. nvtxRangePush("batch_start"); ... nvtxRangePop();

maria: how do you actually pass capture-range? I tried a couple syntaxes and got errors.

devon: one pattern that works for us (wrap NVTX in app) then run: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=nvtx --duration=8s -o out` — behavior depends on nsys version. if that fails, rely on manual start/stop with pid and short duration.

sam: if kernel selection differences are subtle, run a couple traces with identical inputs and compare the kernel timeline in the timeline view instead of raw events. also try `--sample=none` to avoid stack sampling (much smaller) and rely on the timeline + CUDA activity.

maria: good tip. we saw kernel type toggles when batch size crosses a quant boundary so need high-res timeline but small window.

alex: also use `--trace-fork-exec` only if your process spawns helpers; otherwise it bloats capture. use `--uid`/`--pid` whenever possible.

infra-bot: [ci/perf] nightly-kv-bench run completed: https://ci.redwood/pipeline/kv-bench/18025 — artifacts at https://artifacts.redwood/kv-bench/18025 (includes small nsys sample run)

jia: If file size is still too big: 1) reduce duration to <5s and repeat many runs (capture warmup+steady separately), 2) toggle `--sample=none`, 3) convert to `nsys export` to get only kernel timeline CSVs then diffs.

devon: example minimal command I use for quick iterations:

```bash
# warm up in separate run, then short trace for hotspot
nsys profile -o quick-kv \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=none \
  --duration=3s \
  --pid 43210 \
  --force-overwrite
```

maria: thanks — i'll instrument NVTX around the dynamic-window decisions, run warmup and then 3s traces with sample=none and pid filter. will post timeline screenshots.

sam: when you post, include the event timeline and the kernel details table — look for percent time + avg latency for the top kernels (often the quantized matmul kernel shows the shift).

maria: noted. one more Q — any quick way to get a small CSV of kernel names + total time?

devon: `nsys stats -i quick-kv.qdrep --report=cupti_activity` (or use the timeline export) — different nsys versions have slightly different subcommands but `nsys stats` is the path to text reports.

maria: perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:
